title: Why Only Half the Bar Smells Asparagus Pee & Why Cilantro Tastes Like Dish Soap — Benjamin Franklin's 1781 Asparagus-Urine Letter, Pelchat's Cross-Sniffing Matrix & Markt's N = 6,909 Chr-1 OR2M7 GWAS (871 Hits at p < 5e-8), Eriksson's N = 26,455 Cilantro OR6A2 (E)-2-Decenal GWAS, TAS2R38 PAV/AVI Balancing Selection & Human OR51E2 / TAS2R14 / TAS2R46 Cryo-EM (PDB 8F76, 8VY7, 7XP6)

teenKit.tldr: Your sense of taste and smell is completely unique, meaning you and your friends literally inhabit different molecular universes when eating the same food.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Discovering that genetic differences change how we perceive basic flavors shatters the illusion that everyone experiences the exact same reality.
keyTakeaways: Benjamin Franklin wrote a hilarious satirical letter in 1781 about asparagus pee, proving humans have been perplexed by sensory differences for centuries.
A single amino acid swap in your DNA can completely change whether cilantro tastes like fresh herbs or literal dish soap.
Modern structural biology tools like cryo-electron microscopy allow scientists to map human chemoreceptors down to a single angstrom.

vocab.meaning: A Genome-Wide Association Study scans the DNA of thousands of people at once to find genetic variations linked to specific traits like food taste.
Cryo-electron microscopy freezes biological molecules at extreme temperatures to take insanely detailed pictures of them down to single atoms.
A specialized protein on your nerve cells that detects specific chemical molecules in the air or your food and triggers a smell or taste signal.
An evolutionary process where multiple versions of a gene are kept active in a population because they each offer unique survival benefits.

quiz.question: What causes some people to taste soap when eating cilantro while others taste fresh herbs?
options: A genetic variation in an olfactory receptor gene
How much sunlight the cilantro plant received
quiz.explanation: Genetic variations in specific smell receptors, like OR6A2, dictate whether aldehyde chemicals in cilantro register as soapy or herbal.

quiz.question: What historical figure wrote a satirical scientific letter about the distinct odor of asparagus urine in 1781?
quiz.explanation: Benjamin Franklin penned the funny letter while sitting at his private printing press outside Paris.

quiz.question: How detailed can modern scientists map human chemoreceptors using cryo-electron microscopy?
quiz.explanation: Cryo-EM allows researchers to image proteins at sub-nanometer resolutions down to individual angstroms.
